nodes.label: nightly-flakes workflow
nodes.rationale: Answers the two questions a single bun test cannot (#290, #538): are the quarantined suites still broken on hosted runners, and which tests are flaky as opposed to which build was red. 04:00 UTC, after integration (03:00) and integration-brokers (03:30) so the three nightlies do not contend for the same runner minute.

nodes.label: Quarantined suites job (flag off)
nodes.rationale: Runs exactly the three gated suites with ACTOR_TS_SKIP_FLAKY_MNS deliberately absent - stress-test.mjs drops it from the child environment by default, so the job cannot silently degrade into three repeats of six skipped tests. --run-timeout=480000 is stated against timeout-minutes: 30 because the documented symptom is a hang (workers spawn, handshake, never run), so the watchdog is what turns the night into a recorded result rather than a job GitHub killed.

nodes.label: Whole-suite repeat (stress) job
nodes.rationale: Loops the whole suite and aggregates failures by test identity, so this test failed 2 of 5 times is actionable where two red builds a week apart are not. Quarantined suites included, which is the point: excluding them would report a reliable pass rate over exactly the tests known not to be reliable. A test that failed in EVERY repeat is broken rather than flaky and belongs in an issue, not the catalog.

nodes.label: 14-consecutive-green-nights exit criterion
nodes.rationale: Fourteen rather than fewer because the failure is a property of the runner pool, not the code: two calendar weeks spans weekday and weekend pools and several bun-version: latest rolls. Three repeats a night means 42 consecutive green executions. Un-quarantining is one commit: drop the env flag from test.yml, multi-runtime.yml and publish.yml, drop the three describeMns guards, drop bunfig.toml's coveragePathIgnorePatterns, drop --exclude=worker from benchmarks.yml, revisit the pragmatic 80% coverage floor, keep this job as the regression guard. One red night resets the count; greenRuns == runs is the condition and a non-empty runsTimedOut is red regardless. Nothing accumulates the streak - a human counts it, which is the same failure that made the quarantine permanent, and automating it would need actions: read or contents: write in an installing job, which WorkflowHygiene.test.ts forbids.

nodes.label: Both jobs continue-on-error by design
nodes.rationale: The quarantined suites are expected to be red - that is why they are quarantined - and the suite still carries fixed sleeps a stress loop is designed to surface (#418). A red required check for a known-red measurement trains people to ignore it, so the signal lives in the step summary, a ::warning:: annotation and 30-day artifacts instead. Outcome is passed through env:, never pasted into the shell as an expression.
